intro.text:
The largest barrow rises from the hillside like the back of some buried beast. Its stone door has been cracked open, and the earth around it is torn by bootprints, drag marks, and something heavier than any man.
Old grave-charms hang from posts around the mound, but most have snapped. A cold wind breathes from the opening, carrying the smell of wet stone, dust, and extinguished candles.
Sister Maelis stands before the tomb with a lantern in one hand and a funeral bell in the other.
“This was not merely a robbery,” she says. “The tomb was a lock. Something inside has been opened.”
From within the barrow comes a faint scraping sound.
Then a voice, hoarse and terrified, calls from the dark:
“Help me. Please. I did not know what they took.”

outro.text:
At the end of the cold stairs you find a pile of cloth. Just as you thought that the voice must have come from here, the pile starts to move!
A dirty young man with black hair looks at you, he seems very frightened.
"I'am... I was... one of the Grave-Robbers. Orren is my name. I've seen things no one should ever have. They are all dead." He stares at an empty pedestal behind him.
“It was a crown,” he whispers. “Black iron. Gold thorns. They said it belonged to the first king.”
He swallows hard.
“But when we lifted it, something beneath the tomb laughed. Hundreds of Ghosts. They came and took the crown. Then they vanished through the stones. The floor. They are somewhere... below.”

Outside, the clouds part for a moment. On the next hill, where no one stood before, you see a figure in ancient armor watching you.
It raises a rusted horn to its mouth.
